final_recommendation: The room converged on a concrete amendment protocol: Mexico's labor ministry signs binding baseline thresholds (12% union density, wage-theft triggers, weekly facility logs) with an automatic-audit clause enforceable under Chapter 31. Congress, labor, and business all committed to ratification contingent on this signed amendment, which Mexico executed within the meeting timeline.
minority_objections: Canada repeatedly demanded guarantees that the amendment would not trigger reopening of dairy concessions or Chapter 19 dispute resolution
Mexico initially resisted unilateral U.S. congressional veto power and demanded trilateral data-sharing protocols to protect sovereignty
key_conflicts: Congressional Democrats vs. Mexico on enforcement mechanism: unilateral triggers vs. trilateral sovereignty protections
Labor unions vs. business lobby on timeline: labor demanded binding automatic-audit clause before endorsement; business pushed for immediate ratification to lock certainty
Canada vs. all parties on scope creep: insisted amendment be ring-fenced from dairy and Chapter 19 to prevent full renegotiation
key_concessions: Mexico accepted independent inspectors and binding baseline thresholds in exchange for trilateral data protocols and no unilateral U.S. congressional veto
Labor accepted 30-day pilot timeline (down from 14-day demand) in exchange for automatic second-audit clause with no discretion
Business accepted amendment protocol (abandoning ratify-as-is position) in exchange for concrete timeline and Mexico signature commitment
Congress accepted trilateral enforcement structure (no unilateral veto) in exchange for binding numerical baselines and automatic escalation
red_lines: Mexico: no unilateral U.S. congressional veto over enforcement; baseline data must remain within trilateral commission
Labor: no endorsement without automatic-audit clause in binding amendment text, not side letters
Canada: amendment must not trigger reopening of dairy concessions or Chapter 19; must be ratified as separate protocol
Congress: no ratification without Mexico signing binding baseline thresholds and automatic enforcement mechanism in writing
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Implementation capacity: no discussion of whether Mexico's labor ministry has resources to conduct inspections at scale beyond pilot facility
Arbitration backlog: Chapter 31 dispute resolution timeline and capacity not addressed if multiple violations trigger simultaneous audits
Political sustainability in Mexico: domestic backlash risk if U.S. inspectors are perceived as infringing sovereignty, despite trilateral framing
Canadian ratification process: assumed Canada would ratify amended protocol without addressing whether Canadian Parliament would reopen debate on dairy
downstream_risk_variables: Mexico's labor ministry capacity to define and enforce baselines at scale
Chapter 31 arbitration panel composition and timeline for dispute resolution
U.S. congressional whip count stability if Mexico's first pilot inspection reveals widespread violations
Canadian domestic political reaction if amendment protocol is perceived as precedent for future reopening
Business lobby support durability if enforcement triggers supply-chain disruptions or compliance costs
uncertainty_notes: The room achieved convergence on amendment text and Mexico signature, but left unresolved: (1) whether Mexico's labor ministry can scale enforcement beyond the pilot facility; (2) how Chapter 31 arbitration handles disputes over baseline interpretation in practice; (3) whether Canadian Parliament will ratify the amended protocol without reopening dairy debate; (4) whether the U.S. whip count holds if early inspections reveal systemic violations requiring broader enforcement.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congressional Democrats repeatedly stated 'the votes aren't there' without binding enforcement mechanism; drove entire amendment negotiation from R1 onward.
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: Labor unions demanded inspectors, 90-day remedies, automatic-audit clause, and refused endorsement until binding text secured; central driver across all rounds.
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Business conditioned ratification support on certainty and timeline, pushed for 30-day pilot, but accepted amendment protocol rather than driving room toward ratify-as-is.
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Canada repeatedly demanded ring-fencing from dairy/Chapter 19 reopening and required written guarantees, but did not dominate room direction—defensive posture.
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Mexico rejected unilateral U.S. veto, demanded trilateral data protocols, and required sovereignty protections in every round; shaped enforcement mechanism design throughout.
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Media framed narrative shifts but did not drive substantive decisions; participants referenced public narrative only after substantive deals were struck.
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Room treated amendment as necessary to unlock ratification; trade lawyer and all parties acknowledged deal would fail without binding enforcement protocol—drove convergence on amendment path.
